controls.label: Color
controls.qualification: Color from a measured spectrum of the star (Pulkovo catalogue). The disc is unresolved; its darker edge follows a model limb-darkening law, not a measurement.
controls.notes: The color of Fomalhaut's spectrum as the Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue measured it from the ground, 320-1080 nm at 10 nm resolution. No resolved image of the surface is cast; the display axis is celestial north, a convention.

controls.label: Dust ring · ALMA 1.3 mm
controls.notes: The star in the color of its spectrum, with its narrow belt of dust in the belt's own glow at 1.3 millimetres, as ALMA imaged it in December 2015 and January 2016 (project 2015.1.00966.S). It is the ARI-L project's image from the public archive, brought to the resolution of the image MacGregor et al. (2017) made from the same observations and shown in the color scale of their Figure 1. The star's own glow and a galaxy behind the field are removed with the fluxes MacGregor et al. fit, and sky fainter than twice the image noise fades out. The ring is measured on this image: 136 au along its long half-axis, tilted 66.6°, with its centre 14 au north of the star, because the belt is eccentric. The image has no third axis, so the depth is inferred: a tilted ring projects to it better than a spherical shell or a constant depth. Its thickness is the 1° opening angle MacGregor et al. cite, and its east side is drawn nearer, as Kalas et al. (2013) read the starlight the dust scatters; an earlier study tentatively put the west side nearer.
